name: The Inn at Little Washington
positioning: Country inn in Little Washington, Virginia, in the Blue Ridge foothills, founded in 1978 in a former garage, with rooms created by a London stage and set designer and a working farm
best_for: Couples who want a theatrical, design-led country inn
Travelers who want farm experiences, gardens and Blue Ridge hiking alongside a stay

facts.text: The Inn at Little Washington was founded in 1978 in a former garage in a small Virginia town.
The Inn is in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains.
Many hiking trails near the Inn can be reached in Shenandoah National Park via Skyline Drive.
The Inn is in the heart of Virginia's wine country, surrounded by vineyards and wineries.
The guest rooms and suites were created by Joyce Evans, a London stage and set designer.
Conde Nast Traveler says the Inn has rooms and two-story suites, many with balconies and garden views.
Guests can stay in village cottages meant to give the feeling of being residents of the village past.
The grounds include a walled garden with a fountain and a pavilion overlooking the mountains, where guests can enjoy breakfast.
Conde Nast Traveler describes the Monkey Room, where paintings of monkeys line the walls while guests sip cocktails.
Guests can dine in the main Dining Room one evening and at the more casual Patty O's Cafe the next.
Master of Scotch Jeff LaBelle leads intimate Scotch tastings exploring rare bottles.
Conde Nast Traveler reports that doormen greet guests by name at the entry.

highlights.text: In the Goose Walk, Farmer Andy leads a parade of American Buff geese down Middle Street while playing a soprano saxophone.
Conde Nast Traveler says the property spans 24 acres with mountain views, trails, a farm and a chicken coop with a crystal chandelier.
The Inn has a Grecian-inspired pool with private cabanas and poolside food from Patty O's Cafe.
A golf cart tour shows guests the landscape that surrounds the Inn.

considerations.text: The farm micro safari runs Wednesday through Sunday, weather permitting.
WhataHotel notes the small village location requires advance planning for activities.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the exclusive experience.
